---
title: "A page of your own"
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: "#>"
---

rebelrebel draws maps; it does not edit data. A page that lets a reader do something more (mark features, write a
verdict of your own, move a label) is yours, built on the map with two calls: `rr_script()` puts your script into the
page, and `rr_serve(routes = )` gives it routes of its own on the server. The script is given one object, `rr`, the
whole of what it may use of the page (the help of `rr_script()` lists it):

| `rr.` | gives |
|---|---|
| `map` | MapLibre's map |
| `layer(id)` | a layer's MapLibre style ids and source |
| `on("click", id, fn)` | a click on a layer's features, its row as `row()` |
| `setData(id, geojson)` | new data for a layer sent whole |
| `filter(id, key, expr)` | a filter of your own, kept with the page's choices |
| `panel(title)` | a box in the sidebar, yours to fill |
| `fetch(name, init)` | your route `name` on the server; `rr.served` is false in a bundle |
| `save(name, text)` | a file handed to the reader |

## A list of marked positions

A click on a position adds its vessel and time to a list in a panel; a button saves the list. On a server, the list
goes to the route `marks`; in a bundle, which has no server (as on this page), the reader is handed a file.

```{r}
library(rebelrebel)

js <- r"(
  const body = rr.panel("Marked");
  const list = document.createElement("ol"), save = document.createElement("button");
  save.textContent = "Save the list";
  body.append(list, save);
  const marks = [];
  rr.on("click", "positions", async ({ row }) => {
    const r = await row();
    if (!r) return;                       // clicked again meanwhile
    const v = Object.fromEntries(r.map(c => [c.name, c.value]));
    marks.push(v);
    list.append(Object.assign(document.createElement("li"),
                              { textContent: `${v.vid} at ${v.time}` }));
  });
  save.onclick = () => rr.served
    ? rr.fetch("marks", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(marks) })
    : rr.save("marks.csv", "vid,time\n" + marks.map(m => `${m.vid},${m.time}`).join("\n"));
)"

m <- rr_example("trawlsurvey") |>
  rr_point(colour = behaviour, popup = c(vid, time), id = "positions",
           name = "Positions") |>
  rr_script(js)
m
```

Click a few positions, then *Save the list*.

## Its route on the server

Served from R, the route writes what the page sends to a file, a row a mark, never rewriting it. A route's function is
given the request (`method`, `path`, `query`, `body`, a JSON body read into R) and returns what goes back: a list as
JSON. Keep it fast: the server answers one request at a time.

```{r}
#| eval: false
file <- "marks.csv"
rr_serve(m, routes = list(marks = function(req) {
  write.table(req$body, file, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE,
              col.names = !file.exists(file), append = file.exists(file))
  list(saved = nrow(req$body))
}))
```

In a script run by `Rscript`, give `rr_serve(..., wait = TRUE)`: it keeps serving until stopped (Ctrl-C). In
RStudio it answers while the console is idle. The page's writes are answered only for a page opened from this computer.
